Again, this is *such* a big shift. Punishing patients really is that line in the sand. 

SFL is leaving Republicans with a difficult choice ahead of the midterms: do they align themselves with a movement explicitly calling for the punishment of women?

And it's sort of working! Anti-abortion groups in SC that opposed last year's bill are either endorsing or staying quiet on this one. 

But this isn't just about SC—it's a test case for the country: conservatives clearly think they can slowly roll out punishments for patients without anyone noticing

This South Carolina bill actually started as a bill to punish women with murder charges (which in that state can mean the death penalty). 

Not enough Republicans would get on board last year, so punishing women with two years in prison is the GOP's "compromise"—they think it's more palatable

Because remember, I just reported this a few weeks ago!

The last few months have made it obvious: pregnancy-related arrests are on the rise, 'equal protection' bills to punish abortion patients as murderers have been introduced in over a dozen states—and now the groups that promised for years never to punish women are suddenly on board

About a year ago, I warned this was coming—predicting that the anti-abortion movement was fast-tracking a major criminalization push 

jessica.substack.com/p/three-year...

Under SB 1095 in South Carolina, women who have abortions would be punished on misdemeanor criminal charges. 

Even rape victims and those with nonviable pregnancies would face two years of prison time for having an abortion.

Students for Life president Kristan Hawkins calls it "an easy vote"

It was only a matter of time: the powerful anti-abortion org Students for Life has endorsed legislation to imprison abortion patients.

The move marks the biggest shift in anti-abortion politics in decades. jessica.substack.com/p/the-mask-i...

www.politico.com/news/2026/04...

When I say I've been warning about this for years, I mean it. Here's a piece I wrote in 2023 laying out how Republicans would use crisis pregnancy centers to informally ban birth control jessica.substack.com/p/the-gops-p...

They don't name crisis pregnancy centers specifically, but that's exactly what they've been laying the groundwork for. Here's the breakdown I published this weekend jessica.substack.com/p/the-week-i...

I'll have more in tomorrow's newsletter, but the short version is exactly what the Politico headline says: the administration wants to take federal dollars for contraception access for low-income women and give it to groups that focus on "natural family planning methods" and "infertility services"

I've warned for years that Republicans planned to reroute federal family planning dollars to crisis pregnancy centers—groups that won't even talk about birth control. 

I re-upped that prediction just last week. A day later, this Politico piece dropped. 
jessica.substack.com/p/the-white-...

Since the end of Roe, Republicans have been systematically burying maternal death reports and dismantling the committees that put them together. 
 
jessica.substack.com/p/is-florida...

Every local reporter should be calling their town’s CPC and asking where they stand on jailing and executing patients. These are groups that claim to support women! 

Ask how they feel about the nation's biggest network publicly aligning with a movement who wants women dead.

Instead of just noting what a shit show this is and moving on, consider holding your reps responsible: 

Every lawmaker voted to fund CPCs should be asked if they believe taxpayer dollars should go to groups that support executing abortion patients.
